mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines the coefficient of variation (CV) for a data set?
mcqs.explanation: The coefficient of variation is the ratio of the standard deviation to the mean, expressed as a percentage. It measures relative dispersion irrespective of the unit of measurement. Option B states this correctly. Option A reverses the ratio, while C and D use unrelated measures (range and variance).

mcqs.question: For the data set {12, 15, 18, 21, 24}, what is the coefficient of variation (rounded to one decimal place)?
mcqs.explanation: Mean = (12+15+18+21+24)/5 = 18. Deviations from mean are -6, -3, 0, 3, 6; squares are 36, 9, 0, 9, 36; variance = (36+9+0+9+36)/5 = 18; standard deviation = √18 ≈ 4.2426. CV = (4.2426 ÷ 18) × 100 ≈ 23.57%, which rounds to 23.6%. Hence option A is correct. The other options correspond to common rounding or calculation errors.

mcqs.question:
Two data sets are given:
Set A: 50, 55, 60, 65, 70
Set B: 30, 45, 60, 75, 90
Which set shows greater consistency (i.e., lower relative variability)?

options.C: Both sets have the same consistency
options.D: Consistency cannot be determined without more information

mcqs.explanation: For Set A, mean = 60, σ = √50 ≈ 7.07, CV = (7.07/60)×100 ≈ 11.8%. For Set B, mean = 60, σ = √450 ≈ 21.21, CV = (21.21/60)×100 ≈ 35.4%. A lower CV indicates less relative dispersion, so Set A is more consistent. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because the calculations clearly differentiate the variability.

mcqs.question: In a competitive exam, Class X has an average score of 70 with a standard deviation of 5, while Class Y has an average score of 80 with a standard deviation of 8. Which class exhibits less relative dispersion in performance?

options.C: Both classes have the same relative dispersion
options.D: There is insufficient data to compare

mcqs.explanation: CV for Class X = (5 ÷ 70) × 100 ≈ 7.14%. CV for Class Y = (8 ÷ 80) × 100 = 10%. The smaller CV indicates lower relative dispersion, so Class X's scores are more uniformly distributed. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because the CV calculation provides a clear comparison.
